title: *Lebanon's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) - Target Year 2035* (UNDP)
organization: UNDP Lebanon / Government of Lebanon document mirror
limitations: Linked 32.4 MB NDC PDF was identified but not independently parsed in this research session; claims below use only the verified publication-page text.

title: *Lebanon National Adaptation Plan (NAP)* (UNDP)
organization: UNDP Lebanon / Government of Lebanon document mirror
methodology: Official NAP summary describing hazards, sectors, governance, finance, M&E and implementation roadmap
limitations: Linked PDF was identified but claims here are restricted to verified publication-page text rather than unverified PDF page content.

title: *Critical Investments in Key Sectors Can Help Lebanon Mitigate Climate Change Impact on Growth and Prepare for a Green Transition* (World Bank)
geographic_coverage: National; energy, water, transport, solid waste
methodology: CCDR based on quantitative modelling, diagnostics, literature and stakeholder consultation
limitations: Accessible release summarizes the CCDR; underlying climate model/scenario detail was not exposed in the release used for atomic projection claims.

title: *New World Bank Program to Improve Water Supply and Quality and Advance Water Sector Reforms* (World Bank)
geographic_coverage: Greater Beirut and Mount Lebanon; national water reform
methodology: Project design, water-sector diagnostic and reform measures
limitations: Intended project outputs are not evidence of achieved performance.

title: *Lebanon's Recovery and Reconstruction Needs Estimated at US$11 Billion* (World Bank)
methodology: Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment; ground and remote information assembled with government, UN and partners
limitations: Measures conflict damage/loss and recovery needs - not climate damage.

title: *Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project: Frequently Asked Questions* (World Bank)
methodology: Financing and implementation design for recovery of lifeline infrastructure
limitations: Programme architecture and financing are inputs/intended mechanisms, not evaluated outcomes.

title: *Country - Lebanon* operational data portal (UNHCR Data Portal)
organization: UNHCR; IOM DTM data reproduced for IDP measures
limitations: Syrian registration has been suspended since 2015; “active record,” IDP and returnee categories have different definitions and dates.

title: *It's a long road to food security for Lebanon, report warns* (World Food Programme)
methodology: WFP operational account drawing on IPC food-security assessment
limitations: Secondary presentation of IPC findings rather than the full IPC analytical report.

title: *Public Perceptions of Climate Change Risks in Lebanon - Regular Perception Surveys on Social Tensions, Wave 22*
temporal_coverage: Fieldwork Oct-9 Nov 2025; comparison with earlier waves
methodology: 5,002 interviews; weighted sample; 4,670 face-to-face and 332 remote in Bint Jbeil/Marjeyoun
limitations: Self-reported experiences and perceptions; no meteorological attribution and no causal identification of climate effects on tension. Southern access constraints affected mode of interview.

title: *Water as a Tool for Defusing Socio-Political Tension - Executive Summary*
organization: UNICEF Lebanon; AUB-IFI; Search for Common Ground
geographic_coverage: Lebanon; local hotspot evidence including North Lebanon
methodology: Mapping combining socioeconomic, water/environmental and socio-political indicators; programme experience
limitations: Six-page executive summary, not an independent impact evaluation; local project observations cannot establish national causality.

title: *Water Scarcity and Social Tensions in Lebanon: Lessons from the Bcharreh-Denniyeh Case*
organization: ALEF - act for human rights, with Oxfam/SHiFT/Right to Play
methodology: Secondary-source policy synthesis and case analysis
limitations: Advocacy/policy source; many factual claims derive from secondary journalism or other reports. Its claim that the case previews a national trend is not adopted here.

title: *Conflict Sensitivity Guidance for the Food Security and Agriculture sector (FSAS) in Lebanon*
organization: International Alert with FSA Core Group; UNDP-supported
methodology: Workshop, semi-structured interviews, validation meeting and sector best practice
limitations: Guidance/programme theory rather than evaluation; some contextual statistics are reproduced from IPC and perception sources.

title: *Evaluation of Lebanon Host Communities Support Project (2019-2022)*
methodology: OECD-DAC, theory-based evaluation; interviews, 118 FGD participants including 57 women, site observation and document review, triangulation
limitations: Not climate-specific; predates later conflict and 2025 climate policies. Evaluators identify important M&E weaknesses limiting outcome attribution.
